title: Events vs Commands
summary: Events state facts that happened; commands request work to be done.
explain: An OrderCreated event announces a fact. A CreateOrder command asks a system to perform work. Event-driven designs decouple producers/consumers via brokers (e.g., Event Mesh-style topics). You still need schemas, versioning, authorization, and operational tooling.
analogy: A fire alarm (event) vs an order to evacuate zone B (command).
whyItMatters: Mixing commands into 'events' creates hidden coupling and unclear ownership.
mnemonic: NEWSFLASH not PHONE CALL: Events broadcast facts; don't dual-write two editors.
useCases: Greenfield design workshop: decide if “Events vs Commands” is required given constraints (latency, clean-core, team skills).
Partner retries the same order POST — Events vs Commands prevents double billing.
Architecture review board: defend why you accepted residual risk around “Events vs Commands”.
